_: THE single source of truth for every agent. ONE flat list, one row per agent, one line each. The Agent Invocation Gate reads this first on every /agent-name (gates/agent-invocation-gate.md STEP 0). Renderer: roster.html. Deep detail is NEVER stored here — it lives in the agent's own files (super-agents/<slug>/ or agents/<slug>.md) and in git history. registry.json is RETIRED as of 2026-07-25; this file replaced it.
schema: slug | name | class(super-agent|agent|task-specific|retired) | memory(true=holds context across sessions) | status | invoke | default_runbook(what a BARE name fires) | gate_strength(auto|confirm|always-ask) | aka[] | seat | teams[] | lane(ONE line) | home | from(lineage pointer) | accent. ⚠️ NO numeric platform IDs — names and slugs only; rule + precedent in gates/agent-name-collision-gate.md → NAMES, NEVER NUMBERS.
class_note: class = PERSISTENCE, never rank (super-agent-base.md Constitution §6). 'super-agent' = seated persona with a memory bundle. 'agent' = stateless lens. Mira seats by LANE, never by class. An upgrade is a ONE-FIELD edit here, which is why the list is never split by class.
runbook_note: default_runbook = the ONE routine a BARE name fires when no situation is attached (gates/agent-invocation-gate.md). Name + context = normal persona work, never the runbook. gate_strength: auto | confirm | always-ask; UNSET defaults to confirm. A read-only runbook may sit at auto; anything that WRITES must not — and EARN auto, don't assume it (a routine trends to auto once TRUSTED; external-data fetches start at confirm). Most agents have neither field and that is correct — a bare call then just seats them. All three invocation forms count as 'bare' when no situation is attached; the command form only decides whether session-open also runs.
slim_rule: KEEP THIS FILE SMALL — target ~12KB, hard ceiling ~22KB on disk (base64 inflates 4/3 against a ~30KB return cap). Lane is ONE line. This is CORRECTNESS, not tidiness: a file that can't be read whole can't be safely edited, and this file IS the registration path (proven — Dev Dexter shipped unregistered when it hit ~25KB). ⚠️ NEVER STORE THIS FILE'S OWN BYTE COUNT HERE (2026-07-26: did exactly that and was wrong within one commit — a self-describing size is stale the instant anyone edits it). Measure at HEAD from a directory listing. ⚠️ RULES DO NOT LIVE HERE EITHER — this is a DATA file. A rule goes in its gate/hook and this file keeps at most a one-line pointer (Constitution §2). ⚠️ The ~12KB target has NEVER been met since it was locked. ESCALATED for Michael/Dexter: move the target to a number we will hold, or drop `accent`, the fattest remaining non-essential (it also has duplicate values across rows, so it is already not a reliable identifier).
name_uniqueness: A first name is an INVOCATION TOKEN, not decoration. Two agents may never share one, even with distinct display names — check invocation.tokens below, not just the name field. Homophones and one-vowel gaps count (Clio/Cleo); dictation is the real test. A rename changes display_name ONLY; slugs are immutable (Red Rhett lesson) — so after a rename, check whether the SLUG still contains the freed token (the fmp-frank case). Full gate: gates/agent-name-collision-gate.md.

invocation.how: A named call (/session.agent=X, /session-start=X, /x, bare name, nickname) resolves against THIS list, then loads that agent's home directly. NO double-hop through Felix (steward) or Mira (switchboard). Reading this file is not invoking Felix.
invocation.slug_is_a_token: An agent's SLUG is always a valid invocation token even though the map below is keyed by display names and nicknames: '/session-start=memory-maggie' == '/session-start=Maggie'. Resolve a hyphenated token against the slug field before calling it unresolvable. ⚠️ `fmp-frank` is FMP FIONA's slug — it resolves to HER, never to Fold-in Frank.
invocation.command_form_note: The command form chooses whether session-open runs; it does NOT change Mode A vs Mode B. /session-start=X runs session-open Prime THEN embodies; /session.agent=X only embodies.
